Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. PMLR 202, 2023.

contribution.value: FlexGen is a high-throughput offloading engine that runs OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU by aggregating GPU, CPU, and disk memory through linear-programming-based scheduling and 4-bit group-wise compression of weights and KV cache, reaching 1 token/s with effective batch size 144.

ev.quote: We present FlexGen, a high-throughput generation engine for running LLMs with limited GPU memory. FlexGen can be flexibly configured under various hardware resource constraints by aggregating memory and computation from the GPU, CPU, and disk. By solving a linear programming problem, it searches for efficient patterns to store and access tensors. FlexGen further compresses the weights and the attention cache to 4 bits with negligible accuracy loss
We use two tasks to show that our approximation methods exhibit negligible accuracy loss: next-word prediction on Lambada (Paperno et al., 2016)
language modeling on WikiText (Merity et al., 2016)

We tested the interaction of FlexGen and HELM (Liang et al., 2022) by evaluating a new model OPT-IML-30B (Iyer et al., 2022) ... FlexGen finishes the benchmark of 7 representative sub-scenarios in 21 hours

ev.quote: we present FlexGen, an offloading framework for high-throughput LLM inference. FlexGen aggregates memory from the GPU, CPU, and disk, and efficiently schedules I/O operations, along with possible compression methods and distributed pipeline parallelism.

strengths.value: First system to run OPT-175B on a single 16GB commodity GPU at 1 token/s by aggregating GPU, CPU, and disk memory.

ev.quote: when running OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU, FlexGen achieves significantly higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art offloading systems, reaching a generation throughput of 1 token/s for the first time with an effective batch size of 144

strengths.value: Compresses both weights and KV cache to 4 bits with group size 64 with negligible accuracy loss on OPT-175B (Lambada delta 0.002).

ev.quote: Both methods show negligible accuracy loss compared to FP16. The results reveal the robustness of LLMs against these approximations.

strengths.value: Linear-programming search finds offloading policies proven to be within 2x of I/O-optimal scheduling.

ev.quote: Theorem 4.1. The I/O complexity of the zig-zag block schedule is within 2x of the optimal solution.

strengths.value: Open-source release with full reproducibility and HELM integration that benchmarks OPT-IML-30B in 21 hours.

ev.quote: On the HELM benchmark, FlexGen can benchmark a 30B model with a 16GB GPU on 7 representative sub-scenarios in 21 hours. The code is available at https: //github.com/FMInference/FlexGen.

weaknesses.value: GPU compute utilization is only 13% during decoding because I/O dominates throughput.

ev.quote: The GPU compute utilization is 82% and 13% for prefill and decoding, respectively.

weaknesses.value: 3-bit quantization fails to preserve accuracy, so the method does not extend below 4 bits.

ev.quote: We also tried 3-bit compression but it cannot preserve accuracy.

weaknesses.value: Diagonal block schedule is proven optimal but not implemented because of pre-allocated KV cache buffers.

weaknesses.value: Group-wise quantization adds compression overhead so CPU delegation must be disabled when quantization is on.

ev.quote: Such an overhead could be very significant if run on a CPU which makes the CPU delegation useless, so we turn off the CPU delegation when enabling quantization.

limitations.value: Targets latency-insensitive batched workloads only; high latency (thousands of seconds per batch) makes it unsuitable for interactive use.

ev.quote: We introduce FlexGen, a high-throughput generation engine for LLM inference, which focuses on latency-insensitive batch-processing tasks for resource-constrained scenarios.

limitations.value: Tested only on OPT models; no evaluation of other transformer families like LLaMA or BLOOM despite the claim of generality.

ev.quote: OPT models (Zhang et al., 2022) with 6.7B to 175B parameters are used in the evaluation. Although we do not evaluate other models, the offloading in FlexGen can be applied to other transformer LLMs

limitations.value: No safety, bias, jailbreak, or refusal evaluation after compression; accuracy assessed only on Lambada accuracy and WikiText perplexity.

ev.quote: We use two tasks to show that our approximation methods exhibit negligible accuracy loss: next-word prediction on Lambada (Paperno et al., 2016) and language modeling on WikiText (Merity et al., 2016).

limitations.value: Hardware tested only on data-centre cloud GPUs (T4 / RTX 3090); no Jetson, mobile, or true edge deployment.

ev.quote: We run experiments on the NVIDIA T4 GPU instances from Google Cloud.

future_work_stated.value: Implement the proven I/O-optimal diagonal block schedule with non-contiguous attention computation.

future_work_stated.value: Extend padding strategy with techniques from Orca to handle batches of variable-length prompts more efficiently.
